eu1.title: Trump to meet AI leaders to discuss US investment in their companies
eu1.description: The US president said on Friday he expects to meet the leaders of top AI companies next week.

eu1.title: US stocks slump as fears over Big Tech shake Wall Street
eu1.description: The Nasdaq saw its biggest daily fall since early 2025.

eu1.title: Who can buy shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX?
eu1.description: From next week individual investors can take a stake in Musk's rockets-to-AI company.

eu1.title: Hospitality jobs boom as US prepares for World Cup
eu1.description: It is the third month in a row US jobs figures have beaten expectations.

eu1.title: Is there an AI stock market bubble, and is it ready to burst?
eu1.description: Despite the Iran war, inflation and debt fears, US markets keep hitting record highs, fueled largely by AI. BBC's Samira Hussain looks into whether that bubble will burst.

eu1.title: British Heart Foundation plans to close 150 charity shops
eu1.description: The charity says it is facing "an exceptionally challenging trading environment".

eu1.title: Single 20-somethings need AI to make first move on dating apps - Hinge boss
eu1.description: Jackie Jantos says loneliness and lack of confidence were challenges for young adults looking for relationships.

eu1.title: Final pieces fired at Denby as production ends
eu1.description: "We are so hugely proud of everything this Derbyshire pottery has achieved," the company says.

eu2.title: EU must act before China cripples European industries, warns EPP chief
eu2.description: Countries like France are pushing for a tougher stance against Beijing, arguing that Chinese overproduction is straining an already struggling European economy.

eu2.title: Google rents SpaceX/AI supercomputers for $920M a month, ahead of IPO
eu2.description: Google has signed a $30 billion deal to lease computing power from SpaceX, paying $920 million per month through June 2029. The move came after SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026, gaining massive data centres. The deal precedes SpaceX’s highly anticipated IPO next week.

eu2.title: Pay transparency: Which EU countries are ready for the new rules?
eu2.description: Millions of Europeans still apply for jobs without knowing how much they pay. New EU rules aimed at boosting salary transparency and tackling the gender pay gap were due to take effect by 7 June, but most member states are set to miss the deadline.

eu2.title: Trade commissioner pledges ‘new tool’ to diversify suppliers and cut reliance on China
eu2.description: The European Commission is preparing a new tool to curb the bloc's dependence on China, with Trade Chief Maroš Šefčovič saying on Friday that companies could be required to source from at least three different suppliers.

eu2.title: Smart pipelines: Can AI protect the world’s energy lifelines?
eu2.description: As ageing pipelines face growing risks, the energy industry is increasingly turning to AI and smart monitoring systems to improve their safety and efficiency.

eu2.title: Eurozone economy shrinks by 0.2% in the first quarter of 2026
eu2.description: The 21-member euro area has entered negative territory for the first time in over a year, with a dramatic Irish contraction masking more nuanced performances across the bloc's major economies.

eu2.title: Greece gets green light to repay €6.95bn of bailout loans early
eu2.description: Greece has been cleared to repay almost €7bn of bailout loans ahead of schedule, in a move European officials say will improve the country's debt position.

eu2.title: Anthropic calls for ‘brake pedal’ before AI develops itself without human oversight
eu2.description: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said AI agents might soon be able to build and train models themselves and, if that happens, humans could lose control over AI systems.

eu2.title: Global steel crisis deepens as oversupply reaches alarming levels, OECD warns
eu2.description: The global steel industry is facing a growing crisis as subsidised production and excess capacity continue to distort markets, according to the OECD. It says state-backed steel production, particularly in China, is increasing pressure on producers in Europe and other OECD economies.

eu2.title: Hong Kong wants to be a bridge between Central Asia and Chinese businesses
eu2.description: High-level Hong Kong delegation visited Kazakhstan and offered new partnership in several economy sectors including professional services for companies attempting to enter respective markets.

eu2.title: US eyes stake in Azerbaijan's pipelines as economic ties enter new phase after Trump-brokered deal
eu2.description: Washington wants in on Azerbaijan's pipelines and energy infrastructure, a senior US official said in Baku, as the two countries deepen economic ties following Trump's White House peace deal with Armenia.

eu2.title: Remy Cointreau posts 35% profit drop, shares jump on recovery hopes
eu2.description: French drinks group Remy Cointreau reported a 35% drop in full-year net profit on Thursday as tariffs slammed sales in its key China and US markets. Despite this, shares soared more than 10% on Thursday morning.

eu2.title: AI giant Broadcom sheds $300bn in market value as outlook misses sky-high expectations
eu2.description: The American chipmaker Broadcom reported a 48% revenue surge and AI semiconductor sales up 143%, but it disappointed investors by not raising its long-term sales target, sending shares tumbling more than 12% in after-hours trading.

eu2.title: Amazon pledges €10 billion for Europe with 25,000 new jobs and warehouse robots
eu2.description: Amazon is making one of its biggest new bets on Europe, announcing more than €10 billion in investments to expand and modernise its warehouse and delivery network across the continent over the coming years.

eu2.title: SpaceX sets IPO price, valuing company at $1.75tn ahead of record debut
eu2.description: The company said on Wednesday that it plans to list its shares at $135 each. The offering would value SpaceX at around $1.77tn (€1.56tn), making it one of the world's most valuable listed companies and potentially the largest IPO in history.

eu2.title: Energy transport corridors to Europe boosted by AI and new digital systems
eu2.description: AI and new digital technologies are key to the urgently needed alternative energy trade routes through the Southern Gas Corridor and the Middle Corridor systems connecting the Caspian and Europe.

mid1.title: Bolivia’s legislature passes law allowing use of troops against protesters
mid1.description: New law grants president power to use military to clear roadblocks set up amid weeks of antigovernment demonstrations.

mid1.title: Nigerian forces rescue 360 captives from Boko Haram
mid1.description: Nigerian forces rescued 360 captives, including women and children from a Boko Haram mountain hideout in Borno State.

mid1.title: Trump says will not unfreeze Iranian assets before ceasefire deal reached
mid1.description: Iranian officials have indicated the release of funds would build 'trust' needed to reach lasting deal ending war.

mid1.title: Police say two suspects have been shot and killed in Israel gun attack
mid1.description: Police say two suspects have been shot and killed in Israel gun attack.

mid1.title: Al Jazeera reports from Beirut after Israeli attack
mid1.description: Multiple explosions have hit Beirut’s southern suburbs as Israel launches new attacks, claiming to target Hezbollah.

mid1.title: People flood Madrid streets to see Pope Leo’s flower-carpeted procession
mid1.description: Pope Leo XIV hails Spain’s ‘school of faith’ at Madrid Mass, urges unity amid vast Corpus Domini crowds.

mid1.title: Authenticity is what American voters want
mid1.description: Results in US Democratic primary races are showing that old establishment politics no longer work.

mid1.title: Kimi Antonelli wins delayed Monaco Grand Prix to extend F1 lead
mid1.description: Antonelli takes his fifth successive Grand Prix win in race interrupted by crashes after asphalt breaks apart.

mid1.title: Ronaldo, other ageing stars push limits to make history at World Cup 2026
mid1.description: Experts say sport science is just part of a complex system of factors needed to extend longevity in football.

mid1.title: From online class to Revolution Square: A Tehran teacher’s routine amid war
mid1.description: Al Jazeera follows a teacher who navigates a new life marked by a weak internet, soaring prices, and solidarity rallies.

mid1.title: Iran’s World Cup squad lands in Mexico amid US visa row
mid1.description: Iranian delegation arrives at their World Cup base camp a day after several members were denied visas by the US.

mid1.title: Iran’s World Cup team arrives in Mexico as US visa row continues
mid1.description: Iran’s national football team has arrived in Mexico ahead of its World Cup matches in the US.

mid1.title: Does Israel really think it can get rid of Hezbollah in Lebanon?
mid1.description: It’s hard to assume that ‘anything positive’ for Lebanon can come from its talks with Israel, argues analyst Imad Harb.

mid1.title: The Taiz transplant team looking to begin a medical revolution in Yemen
mid1.description: Taiz's Cardiac and Vascular Diseases and Kidney Transplant Center provides Yemenis with affordable treatment.

mid1.title: Peru polls open in Keiko Fujimori, Roberto Sanchez presidential run-off
mid1.description: Race between right-wing Fujimori and left-wing Sanchez follows first round of voting marred by logistical issues.

mid1.title: Army frees 360 people abducted by Boko Haram in Nigeria’s Borno state
mid1.description: Two infants succumbed to the 'harsh conditions' of Boko Haram captivity in the Mandara mountains, says army.
